values: Seven specified nutrients are audited. Fibre is excluded from calculations, completeness counts and status criteria.

150 active recipes and all 857 ingredient lines are represented line by line in Ingredient Audit. The second pass removes one invalid syrup proxy; totals for those recipes are incomplete until a valid CoFID profile is agreed.
RenalPlan active recipe data: data/RecipeData/breakfasts.ts, lunches.ts, dinners.ts.
Official Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset 2021. The GOV.UK page says this version was updated 19 March 2021.
Nutrient values were read from the official Excel workbook; each ingredient row records Food Code plus Proximates, Inorganics and Factors worksheet row numbers.
The guide says nutrient values are per 100 g, Tr is trace, and N means present in significant quantities but no reliable amount is available.
Energy, protein, available carbohydrate, fat, sodium, potassium and phosphorus are audited. Fibre is excluded from this audit.
Per-ingredient contribution = nutrient per 100 g × converted ingredient grams ÷ 100. Recipe numeric subtotal per serving = sum of ingredient contributions ÷ recipe servings. Fibre is excluded.
Ingredient Audit contribution columns and Nutrient Comparison.

The stated gram value is used as the edible ingredient/input weight. No extra edible-proportion multiplier is applied because CoFID nutrients are per edible food portion, and a recipe grams field is treated as an edible/prepared amount unless explicitly marked otherwise.
CoFID user guide, Factors worksheet discussion: edible conversion factor applies when inedible waste is included in the weight. Factors are recorded in Ingredient Audit but not applied.

Millilitres were converted to grams using CoFID specific gravity when available; otherwise 1.00 g/ml is used and flagged. Spoon quantities use line-specific household weight assumptions recorded in Ingredient Audit, such as oil 4.6 g/tsp, lemon juice 5 g/tsp, honey 7 g/tsp, and stated herb/spice estimates. CoFID does not supply those spoon weights.
CoFID 1.2 Factors; spoon volumes/weights are labelled assumptions in Ingredient Audit.

Where the recipe gives an unweighed whole item, the audit uses labelled assumptions: whole egg 50 g edible, egg white 33 g, English muffin 60 g, bagel 85 g, wrap 60 g, bacon rasher 20 g, lettuce leaf 10 g, herb sprig 1 g.
Ingredient Audit “Weight conversion / assumption”. These are not CoFID-specific portion weights.
232 of 857 ingredient lines require household or unit weight estimates. Their contribution is calculated but the line is marked estimated.

Exact names, accepted standardized CoFID equivalents, conditional profiles and unmatched foods are distinguished line by line. Every matched line includes CoFID Food Code, exact CoFID food name and worksheet row references. Maple syrup has no accepted CoFID 2021 match; the first-pass golden-syrup substitution was removed.

Tr is treated as zero only in numeric subtotal and counted in its own column. N and blank cells are not treated as zero; the known numeric subtotal is shown, while difference is left blank if any ingredient cell is N/blank for that nutrient.

Dry/raw ingredient weights use raw or dried CoFID profiles. A prepared CoFID profile is used where the recipe explicitly gives a cooked quantity or method-specific prepared ingredient. Where cooking water is drained and the raw/cooked weight basis or nutrient retention is not clear, the meal remains unresolved.
Current stored nutrition values after the supported B008 correction. Previous B008 values and the field-by-field changes are in the change log.

Difference = CoFID numeric subtotal per serving minus the revised stored recipe value. Difference percent = difference ÷ revised stored value. Fibre is excluded. Differences are not calculated for incomplete CoFID nutrient totals.

Second-pass Verified requires all seven audited nutrient comparisons complete, accepted exact or standardized food matches, no unresolved cooked/drained weight basis, and each difference within ±10% using the disclosed portion assumptions. Fibre is excluded. This verifies the calculation under those inputs. The 10% band is a QA screen, not a clinical or regulatory tolerance.

Nine discrepancies remain: six recipes list less fat than the vegetable oil alone; D023 and D040 have potassium below conservative boiled/drained scenarios; and L028-L030 likely overstate potassium because potato cooking water is discarded. These values remain unchanged because exact recipe-specific cooking losses or oil retention are not established.
Recipe Status and Potato K Review.
Used when a conditional food profile, absent CoFID row, N/blank cell, unmeasured product/portion or cooking-water yield prevents a defensible verified total.

The app labels the value “phosphate”. CoFID provides elemental phosphorus. Comparisons assume the app field means mg elemental phosphorus; the project data do not establish whether the app instead intended phosphate-ion mass.
Nutrient Comparison and the app Nutrition field.

Bethke & Jansky report boiling potato cubes reduced potassium by 50% and shredded potatoes by 75%. The potatoes in the recipes are cut and boiled, but exact piece size and weight basis are not specified.

A 2025 study reports potassium retention ranging from 54% to 74% across boiled potatoes under varied temperature-rise conditions. This supports a broad sensitivity range, not a recipe-specific correction.

L025-L027 use raw input potato composition because their 200 g amount is stated before microwave/baking; the cooked CoFID row at the same grams would mix raw weight with cooked composition. L028-L030 and D023/D040 boil cut potatoes and discard water; cooked/drained CoFID scenarios and published retention ranges test direction only, not an exact recipe correction.
Potato K Review; CoFID food codes and Inorganics worksheet row references appear in scenario lines.

Chicken breast uses CoFID chicken light meat, raw (18-290, Proximates and Inorganics row 702); pan-cooked back bacon uses back bacon, dry-fried (19-498, row 72); boiled eggs use whole egg, boiled (12-940, row 1091); baking potatoes use the closest raw old-potato flesh-only row (13-489, row 2235), with skin retained flagged as a limitation.
Fibre is excluded from the revised audit calculations, completeness statistics and status criteria. Fibre fields and calculations in the RenalPlan application are unchanged.
